#### 1. immunodeficiency 61  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.464)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8856825)

**Proposed mechanism:** UBQLN2 (HGNC:12494) —DISRUPTS→ Protein aggregation clearance (GO:0000283); UBQLN2 (HGNC:12494) —BINDS→ Ubiquitinated protein aggregates (CHEBI:61926); Ubiquitinated protein aggregates (CHEBI:61926) —LEADS_TO→ Protein aggregation clearance (GO:0000283); Protein aggregation clearance (GO:0000283) —LEADS_TO→ Motor neuron degeneration (HP:0007244); SH3KBP1 (HGNC:10670) —DISRUPTS→ Immune cell signaling and trafficking (GO:0007242); Immune cell signaling and trafficking (GO:0007242) —LEADS_TO→ Immunodeficiency (HP:0002705); Protein aggregation clearance (GO:0000283) —INCREASES→ Immune cell signaling and trafficking (GO:0007242). Mutations in UBQLN2 disrupt protein aggregation clearance pathways, leading to motor neuron degeneration in ALS15. Similarly, mutations in SH3KBP1 impair immune cell signaling, causing immunodeficiency. The convergence is hypothesized through the accumulation of ubiquitinated protein aggregates (n7), which can non-specifically disrupt broader cellular processes including immune signaling pathways (n5) in addition to their primary role in neuronal protein quality control.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that loss-of-function variants in UBQLN2 do not lead to accumulation of ubiquitinated protein aggregates, or that SH3KBP1 variants do not impact immune cell signaling pathways in cellular or animal models. _(variant: rs113940587)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting common pathways in protein quality control and cellular signaling could offer therapeutic strategies applicable to both neurodegenerative and immune disorders, potentially leading to novel treatments for seemingly disparate diseases.

Loss-of-function mutations in TP53 disrupt the cellular response to DNA damage, leading to motor neuron degeneration in ALS15. Concurrently, TP53 dysfunction impairs cell cycle regulation, contributing to the development of hepatocellular carcinoma.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of TP53 mutations in well-characterized cohorts of ALS15 patients and hepatocellular carcinoma patients, or the identification of distinct, non-overlapping pathways causally linking other genes to these diseases. _(variant: Exclusion of pathogenic TP53 variants with allele frequency > 0.01 in gnomAD for both diseases.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting TP53 pathways or its downstream effectors could offer novel therapeutic strategies for both amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, potentially addressing shared mechanisms of neurodegeneration and oncogenesis.

Mutations in UBQLN2 disrupt neuronal protein homeostasis, leading to ALS. Similarly, mutations in AVP also disrupt neuronal protein homeostasis (specifically affecting vasopressin synthesis and release), leading to neurohypophyseal diabetes insipidus. The shared convergence on neuronal protein homeostasis forms the mechanistic link.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of any shared pathway disruption between UBQLN2 and AVP function in neuronal protein homeostasis, or if mutations in AVP do not affect neuronal protein homeostasis in a manner that could impact general neuronal function. _(variant: rs75601072 (UBQLN2 c.473G>A, p.Arg158Gln) has a GnomAD allele frequency of 0.0001, consistent with a rare disease variant.)_
